name: WATERFALL
considered: A grid of small cells, always drawn (unlit cells are a dim cell, so the grid is always visible). SPECTROGRAM: frequency across, time down; the grid scrolls smoothly a few pixels per picture (the engine's copy, gfx_scroll_down) at a set pixel speed and each new row enters cell by cell from the top edge; a cell's brightness follows its band's level in three steps. ZONES: the grid keeps still, split into 4 x 4 regions (bass top-left to treble bottom-right in reading order), each region one band that fills from its centre outwards as the level rises (a heat map). DUST: the same still grid with the bands scattered at random over the cells. A Player 2 test of the pack framework: the drawing code exists only in its pack (meter_pack_waterfall_grid.c); the firmware carries a stub that says so. SPARKLE: the still grid; a band that jumps well above its own running average (an onset: a hit, a pluck) lights a burst of cells around its column, which fades back to dim in three steps over the Fade time; silence and sustained notes light nothing.

params.label: Scroll speed
params.note: pixels per second, whatever the cell size

params.label: Gain
params.note: how bright the grid is for a given level

params.label: Cell size
params.note: the cell is this many pixels square, with one pixel between cells

params.label: Fade time
params.note: how long a flash takes to fade back to the dim grid
